Hacknet is an immersive and thrilling journey into the dark underbelly of the internet. Its unique gameplay, engaging puzzles, and gripping mystery offer a refreshing and original experience that stays with you long after the credits roll. While the learning curve might be steep and the story somewhat limited, the sense of accomplishment you get from cracking a secure network and the excitement of uncovering online secrets make Hacknet a truly rewarding adventure. So grab your digital crowbar, boot up your terminal, and prepare to unleash your inner hacker - just remember, with great power comes great responsibility (and the potential for a few digital black eyes along the way).

-={ GAMEPLAY }=-
Unique terminal-based gameplay: Master the command line, crack encrypted files, and exploit vulnerabilities as you infiltrate secure systems. It's not just a game, it's a crash course in hacking basics.
Gripping mystery narrative: Unravel a multi-layered conspiracy through emails, chat logs, and stolen files, slowly piecing together the truth behind a powerful corporation's dark secrets.
Authentic hacking atmosphere: The terminal interface, realistic tools, and technical jargon make you feel like a genuine hacker, even if you're not one in real life.
Engaging puzzles: Each network presents a unique challenge, demanding logical thinking, strategic planning, and a bit of trial-and-error to overcome.

Steep learning curve: The terminal-based gameplay can be intimidating for newcomers unfamiliar with coding or command lines.
Repetitive tasks: Some hacking sections involve performing similar actions repeatedly, which can feel tedious at times.
Limited story scope: The narrative, while captivating, can feel short-lived, leaving some players wanting more.

A really fun experience for people who like programming and/or cybersecurity. 

It breaks the fourth wall in a few different ways and has a surprisingly good story with some decent character building. The gameplay can feel repetitive, which is naturally going to happen considering what the game is simulating. Still, each situation thrown at you is unique enough that it generally doesn't overstay its welcome. 

Some of the later missions in the game can be really tricky, requiring a lot of attention to detail and investigation. There's a lot of depth and strategy that isn't immediately obvious. It never feels unfair though, the next step is always a logical one.

The graphics are also really neat, I like the combination of old-school Unix terminal and trippy fractal/abstract animation. It goes a long way to making it feel like I'm plugging into some hi-tech virtual machine.

Definitely my favorite hacking simulator. Very cool base game and DLC experience, plus extensions/custom campaigns allow for pretty much limitless potential.
